subject.title: feat(android): add Wear OS phone proxy

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor and land the first-party phone-proxy transport as an independent Wear OS stage before the watch application and end-to-end UX are ready?
rationale: The patch is a technically coherent foundation, but it establishes a new first-party platform and privileged device transport without independently delivering user-visible watch functionality; repository policy and the linked issue reserve that product/security boundary for human approval.

options.title: Sponsor The Staged Proxy
options.body: Approve the phone-owned architecture and merge this stage after paired-device proof, security signoff, rebase, and required Android gates.

options.title: Review End To End
options.body: Defer transport landing until the watch application can be reviewed and proven with the protocol as one complete user workflow.

options.title: Pause First-Party Wear
options.body: Keep the exploration external or close the staged effort if OpenClaw does not want to own Wear packaging, lifecycle, and release support.

recommendation.title: Sponsor The Staged Proxy
recommendation.body: Approve the phone-owned architecture and merge this stage after paired-device proof, security signoff, rebase, and required Android gates.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the staged architecture issue and integrated the new boundary into the Android runtime, making them the clearest available owner for the sponsorship choice.
